title: Territory latency budgets and adaptive threshold routing
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: We currently observe tail-latency spikes and uneven region load during partial outages. Existing geo-pin and simple latency-based routing are brittle when capacity shifts (maintenance, preemption) and can either over-shed traffic or cause latency SLO violations across tenants. Goal: design and implement a territory-aware, latency-budget-driven routing policy that combines per-territory latency budgets, soft geo-pinning for session affinity, and adaptive capacity thresholds that wire into circuit breakers and graceful load shedding. The policy should prioritize SLO attainment (p95/p99), minimize cross-territory cold-falls, and allow controlled cost trade-offs (prefer higher-cost region only if budgeted).
acceptance_criteria: Define per-territory latency budgets and map them to routing tiers (local, regional, fallback)
Implement adaptive thresholding that uses regional capacity signals (GPU utilization, queue depth, contention score) to adjust steering weights in real-time
Circuit breaker integration: register region-level CBs with three states (Closed, Tripped, Draining) and expose metrics and events to Console
Load shedding policy that respects customer-configured SLO priority and provides graceful degradation (response truncation / reduced max tokens / degraded model variant) when shedding is necessary
End-to-end tests and canary rollout that demonstrates p95 and p99 improvement for a representative workload and no regression for pinned sessions
Dashboard showing per-territory budgets, current budget spend, CB state, shed events, and rollback triggers
tasks: Draft latency-budget model and mapping to routing tiers (Ava)
Add telemetry hooks for capacity signals: GPU util, queue depth, avg K/V hit ratio (Diego)
Implement adaptive steering controller with smoothing and hysteresis (Eng runtime team)
Extend circuit breaker service to support Draining state and region-level metrics (Infra)
Implement graceful load-shedding adapter with per-customer policies (Platform)
Add Console widgets and alerts for territory budgets and shed events (Console)
Write integration tests + failure injection harness (SRE)
Canary rollout: start with 5% traffic for low-risk tenant group, run 72h observation window
decisions: Use territory (country grouping) instead of strict region for budget accounting to reduce noisy failures across AZs
Primary steering signal is a latency budget deficit metric = (allocated_budget_ms - observed_ms) aggregated to territory
Adaptive thresholds will use exponentially-weighted moving averages with a 60s half-life and a 3-minute hysteresis window to avoid flapping
When CB enters Draining state route new requests off-region but allow existing KV sessions to finish to avoid inconsistency
Load-shedding actions ordered: reduce max_tokens -> switch to quantized model variant -> return structured 503 with suggested retry-after
Default SLO tiers: Gold(p95<120ms), Silver(p95<220ms), Bronze(p95<400ms) — customers can configure
open_questions: What telemetry threshold maps to a CB transition from Closed -> Tripped? (proposal: 3x p99 latency breach over 5m)
Do we allow per-tenant override of territory pinning? (security/consistency trade-off)
How should cost-aware routing penalize regions with higher egress or GPU spot risk? (weight decay vs hard budget)
Fallback model selection: prefer higher-latency but cheaper region or lower-latency expensive region for Gold tenants?
